title: Interactive Cross-modal Learning for Text-3D Scene Retrieval

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Abstract says IDeal "completely solves the alignment challenge" and achieves "near-perfect retrieval accuracy," but the best reported R@1 values are 37.8, 26.4, and 20.2 on ScanRefer, Nr3D, and Sr3D (Table 1), and the Limitations section admits the method's performance is "relatively low." This is an overstatement contradicted by the paper's own results.

The paper defines ρ(v_i) = 1 / (average k-NN distance + ε), which is a density estimate: dense regions have small average distance and thus large ρ. It then says multiplying similarity by √ρ ensures "high-density regions receive appropriately reduced similarity scores." In fact, large ρ increases the similarity score for high-density regions, the opposite of the stated goal. The inverse factor should be used if the goal is to downweight dense regions.

The minimum enclosing hypersphere constraint is written as "u_i^j o_i^T ≤ R_i, ∀j." This is a dot-product inequality, not a hypersphere condition. The correct constraint is ||u_i^j - o_i|| ≤ R_i (or ||u_i^j - o_i||^2 ≤ R_i^2). As written, the equation does not describe a sphere centered at o_i.

Eq. (7) uses log S(ũ_i, v_j) as a loss term, but S is consistently used elsewhere as a similarity/logit, not a probability (e.g., Eq. (3) applies softmax to S). If S is a cosine similarity, it can be negative, making log S undefined. The loss should use log ŷ or a normalized probability, not log S.

The fusion equation is written as "u_i^j = α u_i^j + (1−α)u_i^{j−1}". This is self-referential: the same variable u_i^j appears on both sides. Algebraically it degenerates to u_i^j = u_i^{j−1} (unless α=1), which contradicts the intended fusion of the new response. It should use the newly encoded response feature, e.g., α f_r(a_i^j) + (1−α)u_i^{j−1}, with a new symbol for the fused feature.

Table 2 lists the no-dagger RoMa baseline as ScanRefer 9.7/33.1/50.2/93.0 and Nr3D 8.3/27.9/37.2/73.4. Table 1 lists the same RoMa coarse-grained setting as ScanRefer 11.4/34.8/54.4/100.6 and Nr3D 6.5/24.8/37.6/68.9. The Table 2 ScanRefer values are exactly the VSE∞ row values, indicating a copy/paste error.

Table 1 IDeal† reports ScanRefer 37.8/71.8/86.4/196.0 and Nr3D 26.4/62.7/78.7/167.8. Table 2 RoMa+IDeal† reports the same ScanRefer values, 37.8/71.8/86.4/196.0, but different Nr3D values: 25.4/60.7/75.7/161.8. For the same configuration the Nr3D numbers cannot differ, so at least one of these entries is inconsistent.

The text cites "[44, 60]" and then inserts a full reference "[60] Zhang, L., Wang, M., & Liu, Q. (2022). Bayesian Density Correction for Cross-Modal Retrieval. In Proceedings of ICLR 2022." However, the reference list contains entries only up to [59]; there is no entry for [60]. This is a nonexistent/invented citation or a serious reference-list omission.

The sentence "Some other attempts [8, 13, 14] have proposed interactive cross-modal retrieval frameworks that incorporate LLMs and VLMs" attributes [14] to interactive retrieval. Reference [14], "Learning to Rematch Mismatched Pairs for Robust Cross-Modal Retrieval," is a noisy-correspondence/robust cross-modal matching paper, not an interactive LLM/VLM retrieval framework. The citation appears to be misattributed.
